A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same speech-decoding work. All 16 pages of each version, including the figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–D, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original MEG experiments on speech detection, voicing classification, pretext-task ablations, data scaling, dataset aggregation and novel-subject generalisation.

after.justification: v5 retains those original empirical results and adds an EEGPT speech-detection comparison in Table 2.

M1.justification: The architecture, three pretext tasks, losses and downstream linear probing remain unchanged. Section 3.2 newly specifies ρ ∈ [0, 0.5], but both versions already report the same experimental values in Table 4: 0.5 for phase and 0.2 for amplitude. This documents the method more explicitly without establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use Cam-CAN and MOUS for pretraining and the Armeni and Gwilliams MEG datasets for downstream speech detection, voicing classification and subject-generalisation evaluation. EEGPT is evaluated within existing coverage; no dataset, task or test population is added.

E2.justification: Table 2C adds EEGPT plus a linear classifier, citing Wang et al. (2024), alongside the retained BIOT and BrainBERT comparators. The existing tabulated comparison methods remain present.

E3.justification: The added EEGPT evaluation uses publicly released EEG-pretrained weights and concatenated groups of 19 sensors, as described in Section 4.2 and Appendix A. Existing splits, preprocessing, metrics, training hyperparameters and Table 2C's reduced-data restrictions remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The individual-pretext-task and smoothing ablations in Table 2B, scaling analyses, novel-subject tests and dataset-aggregation analysis are retained unchanged. The added EEGPT benchmark comparison does not introduce a new ablation, robustness test or supplementary analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report standard errors over up to five seeds, vary sampled pretraining subjects across seeds, and use one-sided t-tests with p < 0.05. EEGPT follows the existing uncertainty-reporting practice; no change in run counts or statistical procedures is stated.

E6.justification: Table 2C adds EEGPT at ROC AUC 0.602 ± 0.006. Corresponding scores for the proposed method (0.705 ± 0.003), BIOT (0.615 ± 0.002) and BrainBERT (0.556 ± 0.007) remain unchanged. Section 4.2 removes the qualitative report that training BIOT on MEG failed to exceed chance. Existing scaling and aggregation results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix B newly asserts that transforming a fraction ρ ≥ 0.5 has the same effect as transforming 1 − ρ with the complementary amplitude or phase shift. This adds a limited mathematical equivalence assertion supporting the explicit parameter range in Section 3.2. No proof is supplied, and Equations (1)–(4) remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about neuroscience-informed self-supervision, heterogeneous-data scaling, novel-subject generalisation, 15–27% baseline improvements and matching quoted surgical decoding performance. EEGPT adds supporting evidence without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 extends the conjectured explanation for BIOT's weaker performance—objectives insufficiently tailored to neural speech processing—to EEGPT. It also drops the failed MEG-training explanation for using BIOT's released weights. The broader scaling interpretations and Section 4.6 limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v5 adds a project-page link, EEGPT's pretrained-weight and 19-sensor adaptation details, and the explicit ρ range. BIOT's pretraining-data description becomes less specific, changing from 'over fifty thousand hours' to a shared description of 'thousands' of EEG hours. Existing hyperparameter, hardware, runtime and licence disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v5 adds Wang et al. (2024), the EEGPT paper, to the references and evaluated-baseline discussion. The remaining cited works and the broader positioning in Section 2 are unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes are localized: acknowledgements and funding disclosures are added, publication and affiliation text is updated, and baseline and parameter explanations are edited. Section order and most prose remain intact. Section 4.2 still says 'two' comparison methods and initially references surgical row 11, although that row becomes 12.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains an EEGPT row, citation and revised numbering. Figure 4 changes its series colors from teal/blue to blue/orange while retaining identical plotted values and error bars. Table captions and front matter receive limited edits, and the acknowledgements shift reference layout.

improvement.justification: The EEGPT evaluation tests the central superiority claim against another pretrained EEG model, with its sensor adaptation documented in Appendix A. Clearer parameter documentation and Figure 4 colors provide additional limited benefits. Removing the failed BIOT-training disclosure and leaving stale Table 2 references reduce transparency and consistency slightly, but the added comparison and documentation support a small net improvement.
